      - article:

      - heading "3. Worked example" [level=3]
      - paragraph: "Two dice are rolled. Let A: “Sum is 7” and B: “First die is 4.” Find P(A ∪ B)."
      - article:
        - text: "Step 1: Counts"
        - paragraph:
          - text: "|A| = 6"
          - text: "|B| = 6"
          - text: "|A ∩ B| = 1"
          - text: "|S| = 36"
      - article:
        - text: "Step 2: Apply the rule"
        - paragraph: P(A ∪ B) = 6/36 + 6/36 − 1/36 = 11/36
      - article:
        - text: Result
        - strong: P(A ∪ B) = 11/36 = 30.56%
      - heading "4. Don’t get tricked" [level=3]
      - paragraph: ✕ Don’t add P(A) and P(B) directly when events overlap.
      - paragraph: ✓ If events are mutually exclusive, P(A ∩ B) = 0.
      - paragraph: ✓ Check counts using a sample space or Venn diagram.
